title: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis: a zero-free half-plane Re s > 11/12 for Dirichlet and Hecke L-functions
summary: Every Dirichlet L-function (ζ included) and every finite-order Hecke L-function of ℚ(√−3) has no zero in Re s > 11/12, by the cubic-theta probe of openai2026quasiRH Part I; with the general library it needs (zero-free half-planes and the continuation principle, power residue symbols as ray class characters, Gauss sums and reciprocity at composite moduli of ℤ[ω], smooth Mellin kernels, uniform Hecke L-function bounds and zero detection, large sieves over number fields, Kubota's character and theta functions with Patterson's cubic theta function, the transfer from abelian fields to Dirichlet L-functions) and the consequences: the zero strip, the conditional least-character bound (log q)^(1/(1−θ)) and the least quadratic nonresidue n(p) ≤ C(log p)^12.

targets.name: QuasiRiemann.zeroStrip_of_zeroFree
targets.statement: If every primitive Dirichlet L-function is zero-free right of θ ∈ [1/2,1), every zero ρ with Re ρ > 0 of a primitive one satisfies 1−θ ≤ Re ρ ≤ θ; same for the primitive finite-order Hecke family of F; at θ = 11/12, 1/12 ≤ Re ρ ≤ 11/12.

tests.name: grh
tests.statement: θ = 1/2 gives Re ρ = 1/2

tests.name: imprimitive
tests.statement: principal mod p: zeros on Re s = 0; excluded

targets.name: QuasiRiemann.leastNonOne
targets.statement: leastNonOne χ = least n ≥ 1 with χ(n) ∉ {0,1} for nonprincipal χ; conditional theorem: zero-free right of θ ∈ [1/2,1) ⇒ leastNonOne χ ≤ C_θ (log q)^(1/(1−θ)); Hecke analogue with N𝔭 ≤ C_{K,θ}(log N𝔣 + 2)^(1/(1−θ)).

api.name: le_q
api.statement: leastNonOne χ ≤ q
